transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... well, I hope I'm in the right place. It's honestly a little silly, and I'm probably overthinking it, but... what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I'm having a hard time just... sitting through things? 

Like, I keep getting up during our sprint planning meetings at work. Or even on really important personal calls, like with my mortgage broker. I know I should just stay put and be professional, but I'll suddenly feel like I absolutely need to get a glass of water right that second, or I'll just decide to go check something in the other room. 

It's not a huge deal, and it's not like I'm trying to be rude or anything! It's just getting a bit embarrassing for me. I hope it's okay that I came in for something like this... is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Have you experienced this need to move around or difficulty staying seated for most of your life, including when you were a child, or is this a more recent development?

Um, well... I guess it's actually been that way for most of my life? I hope that's okay to admit. I mean, I really wasn't a bad kid or anything, I promise! I always understood the schoolwork and tried my best to be good. 

But, um, I do remember back in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes have to move my desk... or just, you know, gently remind me to stay in my seat. I was just always kind of... popping up? And maybe talking a little bit before I was called on. Just eager, I suppose! I also tended to rush through my assignments a lot, even when I totally understood the material. I just always wanted to get to the next thing. 

I really did try to be a good student, though. I hope that makes sense? Is... is that the kind of background information you were looking for?

Beyond the difficulty staying seated and wanting to move quickly to the next task, do you often find that you struggle with making careless mistakes, losing things, or difficulty sustaining focus during tasks that aren't particularly stimulating?

Oh, um... well, I don't really lose things very often, I promise! I try to be pretty organized. And I work really hard to avoid careless mistakes, especially at my job. I always want to make sure I'm doing good work. 

But... I guess maybe the focus part can be a little tricky sometimes? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just slacking off, because I really do try to pay attention. It's just that, well, I can sit down to review a pull request for a coworker, or start reading through those mortgage documents I mentioned, and I go in with really good intentions. But then after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize I'm just sort of... staring at the exact same section? And my brain is off thinking about, like, five completely unrelated things instead of the words right in front of me. 

I always catch myself and get right back to work, of course! I really try to stay on top of things. But... is that what you mean by difficulty sustaining focus? I feel like maybe everyone gets a little distracted like that sometimes, right?
How often would you say that this difficulty staying focused on tasks like your work documents prevents you from completing them on time or causes you to feel overwhelmed?

Oh, um... well, it really doesn't prevent me from getting things done on time! I promise, I always meet my deadlines. I'm very careful about that because I never want to let my team down or hold up a project. I'm actually a pretty reliable developer, I think. 

I guess... sometimes I might have to work a little bit later into the evening to finish things up, just to make sure they're done right, since I had to keep re-reading things earlier in the day. But I don't mind putting in the extra effort! And as for feeling overwhelmed... I mean, maybe just a tiny bit, sometimes? But only because I want to make sure I'm doing a good job. I think it's pretty normal to feel a little stressed about important work, don't you? I really hope it doesn't sound like I can't handle my responsibilities.
When you have these moments where your mind wanders and you have to re-read the same section of a document, how many times throughout a typical workday would you say this happens?

Oh, gosh, um... I don't think I've ever really counted? I hope that's an okay answer. I just haven't kept track of an exact number or anything like that. It's definitely not happening all day long, I promise! I'm usually very dialed into my work, especially when I'm actually writing code. 

If I had to guess... maybe just a handful of times? Like, just a few times here and there, mostly when it's a really, really dry document. I think that's pretty typical for most people, right? Just a few times a day? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just sitting at my desk daydreaming all afternoon, because I'm definitely working hard!

Would you say that your difficulty staying focused is a frequent enough occurrence that it significantly interferes with the quality of your work or your daily life, or is it something you feel you manage quite effectively?

Oh, um... well, I definitely think I manage it pretty well! I mean, I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly. I don't want you to think my work is bad or anything—I still put out really good code! 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe it has caused just a tiny bit of friction lately? I hope that doesn't sound terrible. It's just that, well, sometimes people at work or even my husband at home have had to follow up with me a little more often than they used to about things I said I'd do. And... I guess I just worry sometimes that I'm starting to look like the unreliable one when it comes to planning things or keeping track of tasks. 

I'm really trying so hard, though! I don't want anyone to think I don't care. Do you think it's normal to struggle with that a little bit when you have a lot on your plate? I just hope I'm not doing a bad job at managing it all.

When you find yourself needing to get up and move around during meetings or calls, does this happen because you are feeling restless and bored, or does it happen because you have become distracted by something else and lost track of what you were doing?

Oh, um... it's definitely not because I'm not paying attention! I promise I'm listening to every word on those calls. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them, especially during important meetings. 

It's more just... well, sometimes I get this feeling, like... a sort of pressure inside? Even if I'm sitting perfectly still and looking right at the screen, I just feel this urge that I need to move, or maybe switch to doing something else, or just fidget with my hands. It's almost like I might crawl out of my skin if I don't do *something*, you know? But I really try to hide it so I don't distract anyone else! I hope that makes sense. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?
Looking back, would you say that your internal feeling of needing to move or fidget has been a more constant and disruptive part of your life than the moments where your focus drifts during tasks?

Oh, um... I guess I haven't really thought about it like that before? I hope that's an okay answer. I don't think either of them is, you know, terribly disruptive. I really try my best to keep everything under control so it doesn't bother anyone. 

If I had to compare them... I don't know, maybe they're just about the same? Or maybe neither of them is a huge deal? I just wouldn't want to say one is worse than the other and make it sound like I'm really struggling, because I'm honestly doing okay! I'm sorry, I'm not sure if I'm giving you the right answer here. Do most people find one to be more of a problem than the other? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things correctly.
When you were in school, did you frequently find yourself blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking the question or interrupting others during conversations?

Oh, um... well, I was always a really good student! I promise I wasn't trying to be rude or disrespectful to the teachers or anything. But... I guess I was just, maybe, a little over-enthusiastic sometimes? 

I do remember back in elementary school... um, sometimes the teachers would have to remind me to stay seated. And, well, I guess there were a few times they actually had to move my desk because I was always popping up out of my chair, or... or maybe talking before I was called on. 

It definitely wasn't because I didn't care about the rules! I just... I understood the work, and I think I'd get so excited that I'd just rush through things or blurt things out because I already knew the answer. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker. I always wanted to be a good kid and make the teachers happy! Do you think it's pretty normal for kids to just get a little too eager like that when they know the material?

Looking back at your time in school, did you frequently find yourself struggling to pay attention to long lectures or losing track of your belongings, or was your difficulty primarily limited to the restlessness and blurting out answers that we already discussed?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I always tried really hard to pay attention in class! I was a good student, and I always took careful notes. I didn't want to miss anything important, you know? So I definitely wasn't just spacing out during lectures. 

And as for losing things... well, maybe I'd misplace a pencil or something every now and then, but who doesn't do that, right? I always had my backpack organized and made sure I had my homework ready to turn in. I wouldn't say I struggled with that at all. 

It was really just... like I said, maybe just being a little too eager sometimes. Just the bouncing around a bit and getting too excited to answer. But I always tried my best to be a good listener! I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things were.
In your adult life, do you frequently find yourself failing to give close attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work tasks, despite your efforts to be careful?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I work as a software developer, so... well, I really have to be on top of the details, you know? I always make sure to double-check my code before I send it off to my team. I really pride myself on doing good work and being someone they can rely on! 

I mean, I guess everyone makes a tiny typo every now and then, but I definitely wouldn't say I make careless mistakes or ignore the details. I really try my absolute best to be thorough so I don't create extra work for anyone else. I hope it's okay that I don't really have a problem with that? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're looking for and not leaving anything important out.
